summary: US stocks rallied on 4 November after Democrats won Congress: the Dow rose 3.0%, the S&P 500 1.6% and the Nasdaq 1.4%, with the VIX down 20% to 16.6. Oil fell sharply, Brent about 9% to roughly 94.6 dollars and WTI about 8%, as Iran-war talk eased, and Dutch TTF gas dropped 7%. Power and nuclear names sold off on data-centre worries (Vistra down about 14%) while wind and solar names such as Orsted and First Solar rose. In Asia on 5 November, chipmakers fell sharply (Samsung, SK Hynix and Tokyo Electron each down 5% or more) while Hong Kong rose. The Banxico decision is due 5 November; the Selic was held on 4 November.

reading.summary: The U.S. sanctioned individuals and companies accused of running fraudulent ship registries that helped Iran's shadow fleet evade sanctions, and issued a new warning.

reading.summary: The Coast Guard is considering commercial icebreakers to help keep Northeast ports and waterways navigable during the coming winter.

reading.summary: Propspeed has joined RightShip's program on efficient, sustainable vessel operations; the excerpt notes hull condition affects fuel consumption and emissions.

reading.title: NAPA on why wind-assisted ships need proof of savings, not just a contract
reading.summary: BIMCO's new retrofit addendum sets out how retrofit savings are shared under time charters, targeting the owner-charterer cost barrier to wind-assisted propulsion.

reading.title: Regenerate Outcomes To Protect Buyers With Insurance In Case Of A Carbon Credit Supply Shortfall
reading.summary: Regenerate Outcomes, a program helping farmers improve soil health and generate carbon credits, sells those credits to corporate buyers; the feed excerpt is short.

reading.title: Here's what 'renoa' — the first new fiber in 25 years — feels like

climate.headline: Panama Canal raises Neopanamax draft to 49 feet while preparing for El Nino drought
climate.detail: Gatun Lake is slightly above its 10-year average and daily slots rose to 33 from 15 Oct. The authority is weighing 2027 steps. NOAA's late-October hazards summary flags flood risk in Panama, Costa Rica and Colombia.
climate.source: Panama Canal Authority via Hellenic Shipping News, 5 Oct 2026; NOAA CPC Global Weather Hazards, 22-28 Oct 2026

climate.headline: COP31 opens in Antalya on 9 November with Article 6 carbon-market funding on the agenda
climate.detail: Türkiye hosts, Australia leads negotiations. Leaders meet 11-12 Nov. Items include funding for Article 6.2 infrastructure (shortfall about $8-9 million) and the PACM Supervisory Body report.
climate.source: Abatable analysis of UNFCCC agenda, 27 Oct 2026 (updated 4 Nov)

climate.headline: El Nino floods hit Somalia: 175,000 affected in October, 3.4 million at risk
climate.detail: UN OCHA counts 175,000 affected; the Shabelle River passed its high-flood level. Southern Africa is also unusually wet, with surpluses in Mozambique, South Africa and Madagascar.
climate.source: UN OCHA via FTL Somalia, 1 Nov 2026; NOAA CPC Global Weather Hazards, 22-28 Oct 2026

climate.headline: Australia's Bureau reports record weekly Nino3.4 reading of +2.88C and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole
climate.detail: The Bureau expects El Nino to peak around November-December and persist into autumn 2027. Seas are up to 3C above average in the west, south and south-east.
climate.source: Bureau of Meteorology, Climate Driver Update, 27 Oct 2026
